fields.features_heading: What Your Shipping Workflow Runs Each Day
fields.features_subheading: Shipping automation does the label and tracking work on every order. Carrier contracts and packaging stay your call.
fields.feature_1:
Quotes from every carrier you connect

Connects to EasyPost, Shippo, or a carrier's own API. Each paid order gets quotes from your accounts at your negotiated rates, and the rate picked is saved with the reason.
fields.feature_2:
Shipping rules written as plain sentences

Describe a rule the way you would tell a new hire, such as ship anything over 5 lb by ground. Emergent turns it into code you can read, and each new rule is one more prompt.
fields.feature_3:
Shipments and products in your database

Stores every label, tracking event, and HS code in a database you own. Support sees where a parcel is without opening a carrier site, and finance can total label spend by month.
fields.feature_4:
Exceptions go to a named person

Sends a Slack message or an email when an address fails or a parcel stalls. The alert names the order and its last scan, and it escalates to a second person if nobody answers it.
fields.feature_5:
Peak season with no task cap

Runs every order through the same rules in the week before a holiday cutoff. When volume triples, there is no task cap for the extra label runs to hit, and nothing waits for a reset.
fields.feature_6:
Your shipping code in GitHub

Exports the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can add a regional carrier or edit a rule in code, and the app runs wherever your stack is hosted.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Shipping Jobs Worth Automating First
fields.tab_content_1:
The cheapest label that still keeps the 4-day promise

Hollow Pine Roasters ships coffee from Ohio and promises delivery within 4 business days. When an order is paid, the app pulls quotes from its USPS, UPS, and FedEx accounts. A cheaper rate that would arrive late is skipped. The lowest on-time rate is bought, with the carrier and tracking number saved on the order.
fields.tab_content_2:
135 labels bought before the afternoon pickup

At 2:00 PM on weekdays, the app buys labels for every order paid since the last run. Today that is 138 orders. Three addresses fail the shipping API's check and stay out of the batch while those customers confirm them by email. Teo Marsh, the warehouse lead, gets 135 labels with a packing list sorted by bin.
fields.tab_content_3:
A package stalled for 72 hours goes to one person

Tracking updates arrive by webhook and are saved against each order. If a package shows no new carrier scan for 72 hours, Ines Calder, the support lead, gets a Slack direct message with the order number and last scan location. The customer gets a short delay email in the same hour.
fields.tab_content_4:
A customs declaration for each order leaving the US

Every order to Canada or the UK gets a customs declaration before the label prints. The app fills each line from the product record: description, HS code, origin, and value in US dollars. An order with a product missing its HS code waits for Teo Marsh, and the code he adds is reused on every later order.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up shipping automation on your own carrier accounts, tested on past orders before it buys a live label.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give every product a weight and a box
fields.howto_step_1_des: Count the minutes your team spends each day comparing carrier quotes, retyping addresses, printing labels, and answering where-is-my-order emails. Write down which carrier accounts you pay for and the delivery promise shown on your checkout page.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Link the carrier accounts you already have through a shipping API such as EasyPost, where adding an account gives access to the rates you negotiated with that carrier. Add the warehouse address and each box size you stock, with its inside dimensions.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Record each product's packed weight and the box it ships in. UPS bills a package at the greater of its actual weight and its dimensional weight, which comes from the box size. A light bag of beans in an oversized box can cost more than it weighs.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write each rule as you would explain it to a new packer: the delivery promise, the batch time, how long a parcel may sit without a scan, and who hears about it. Emergent builds the workflow, its tables, and a dashboard your team can open.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Run last week's orders through the rules without buying any labels. Compare the carrier and cost the app picks for each order with what your team bought by hand, and adjust any rule that chose differently before it touches a live order.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Switch on domestic orders first and keep international ones manual for a week. Check the afternoon batch against the packing station's count each day, and read every held address to see why it failed the check.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn on the stalled-parcel alerts once labels run cleanly, then the customs step for orders leaving the US. Each new rule reads the same order and product tables, and an HS code your team adds once is there for the next order.

faq_plan.q: What is the best shipping software?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best shipping software?

prov.original: What is the best shipping software?

faq_plan.a: The best shipping software for your store is the one that quotes with the rates you negotiated with your carriers and handles the countries you ship to. Test each option on a real order before you switch, and check that you can export your shipment history if you leave. Shipping automation you build on Emergent keeps that history in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a shipping automation?
faq_plan.a: Describe the rule in plain English in Emergent's AI automation builder, including who hears when it cannot decide. Emergent builds the workflow and the database behind it, and you connect your shipping API so quotes come from your own accounts. Start with one rule you can check by eye, such as the carrier for a 2 lb box to Arizona.

faq_plan.q: What is the best free shipping app?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best free shipping app?

prov.original: What is the best free shipping app?

faq_plan.a: The best free shipping app is one whose free plan handles your monthly order count and connects to the carriers you already use. Read the plan's limits before you move a store onto it: a free plan that caps labels can force an upgrade in your busiest month. Emergent is free to start, and its free tier covers building and publishing a shipping app of your own.

faq_plan.q: What is the shipping process in a warehouse?
faq_plan.ref: What is the shipping process in a warehouse?

prov.original: What is the shipping process in a warehouse?

faq_plan.a: In a warehouse, an order is picked from the shelves and packed in a box. The box is weighed and labeled, then staged for the carrier's pickup. Software can take over the label step and everything after it, while picking and packing stay physical work. Shipping is one part of ecommerce automation, which also covers order routing and the emails a customer gets after checkout.

faq_plan.q: Does automated shipping work for international orders?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once each product record holds its customs data. USPS requires a fully completed, electronically generated customs form for international mail, and an app that stores each product's HS code and origin can draft that form for every parcel. Run international orders on their own rule, and one missing code then holds a single parcel instead of the whole afternoon batch.

faq_plan.q: What kinds of shipping automation solutions are there?
faq_plan.a: Shipping automation solutions come in four kinds: multi-carrier shipping software, shipping APIs, warehouse hardware such as conveyors, and apps built on a shipping API. Software gives a team one screen for labels and tracking, while an API puts those steps inside the store's own systems. On Emergent, a store can export its app's full code to GitHub on paid plans.

faq_plan.q: Can shipping automation software track inbound shipments from suppliers?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the supplier sends a tracking number: the software can watch an inbound box the way it watches an outgoing parcel and alert the receiving team the day it is delivered. Matching what arrived against what was ordered belongs to procurement automation, which can read the same supplier and product tables.

faq_plan.q: Can an automated shipping system split one order into several boxes?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once you give it a rule for when to split. A rule such as "anything over 20 lb ships in two boxes" gives each box its own label and tracking number, and the delivery email lists both. Products that cannot share a box, such as a glass carafe and loose beans, go on a list the rule reads first.

faq_plan.q: Do automated shipping solutions work with an existing order system?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the order system has an API: the automation reads paid orders from it and writes the tracking number back to the same order. The customer then sees tracking in the order history they already use, and nobody pastes numbers between screens. Check that the API exposes both orders and fulfillment updates before you build.

faq_plan.q: Can automated shipping software reorder boxes when they run low?
faq_plan.a: Yes: each label batch can subtract the boxes it used from a count per box size, and when a size drops below the level you set, the app drafts a reorder. Sending that reorder to the supplier and tracking it to delivery is the job of purchase order automation. Count the shelf once a month and correct the number, because a damaged box never passes through a label run.
